newsitem.title: USA: Schneider sees 1996 sales of $13 bln.
newsitem.headline: Schneider sees 1996 sales of $13 bln.

text.p: Groupe Schneider PA, a global electrical products company based in France, expects to achieve 1996 sales of about $13 billion, Chairman Didier Pineau-Valencienne told Reuters in an interview Tuesday.
Sales expectations would change if the company sold Spie Batignolles, a European electrical construction company that has been on the block since last year.
In late October, Schneider confirmed that Britain's AMEC Plc was in talks over acquiring Spie.

The electrical construction business was not a good fit with the company's long-term strategy, Pineau-Valencienne said. The company plans to concentrate on its two core businesses -- electric ddistribution and electric control and automation.

"Our sales may be about $13 billion this year," said Pineau-Valencienne, who was in Chicago for a National Electrical Manufacturers Association conference. In 1995, the company posted sales of $12.1 billion.

Charles Denny, president of Groupe Schneider-North America, which acquired Illinois-based Square D Co in 1991, said North American year-to-date sales for his division are up five percent. Square D is Schneider's flagship U.S. brand.
In the past three years, the division has enjoyed average sales growth of six percent a year, Denny said. "My goal is to get that up to seven or eight percent a year," he said.
Denny, based in Palatine, Ill., said demand was still strong for the company's electrical products in North America, and he said sales in 1997 could rise by five to seven percent.
